messages.author: 074c5125059cac06
messages.subject: Re: GGIR analysis on cluster
parts:
Hi Emma,

I had the same issue before, and a temporary solution that worked for me was upgrading R to a newer version. When I faced this problem, I was using R 4.2, and after upgrading to 4.4, the error disappeared.

I also recommend using a Docker-based container to run GGIR on a cluster. This approach ensures that the environment is properly configured and helps to avoid errors.

Also I saw you are using

• threshold.in = round(100 * (5/60), digits = 2),
  • threshold.mod = round(2500 * (5/60), digits = 2),
  • threshold.vig = round(10000 * (5/60), digits = 2),

These cutoffs are based on ActiGraph count data. However, since the NHANES 2011–2014 data are in raw acceleration format, you might need to use either the ENMO-based cutoff or include the following options to use cutoffs derived from counts:

  • do.neishabouricounts = TRUE,
  • acc.metric = "NeishabouriCount_x

Xiaoyu
